title: The Meaning of Meaning
subtitle: It carries the weight of each individual; it raises the towering walls of every endeavor.

items.text: May 1987, Plesetsk Cosmodrome
Everything from there on went smoothly and according to schedule. It was a genuine pleasure working with Pointer.
Well, those first days at least.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth, did you go to that ley lines lecture yesterday?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I couldn't make it. I've been reviewing this data for the last 10 hours.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: The model is a mess. Something's off. I can't isolate the issue. It could be the system compiler, or the incantation. Or, maybe we missed some characters when we transcoded it.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Hmm? Oh, the lecture? Yeah, Windsong mentioned it when we met her at the canteen a few days ago. Hold on.
The chair swivels halfway, and Hissabeth stands, stretching before setting her bread aside.
A snake holding a data card slithers up to Pointer's feet.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: This is Hélène. She woke up just a while ago. Hélène, meet Pointer.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We couldn't all attend the lecture, but I asked someone to take Hélène there to observe. Here are the notes.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I still haven't stopped being amazed by your siblings' telepathic connection.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I wonder if there is an arcane skill that might approximate the same effect. Imagine how much faster we'd be able to share information with it.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It's got its advantages, if you're willing to accept eight different voices oscillating between a party and a brawl every day in your mind.
Hissabeth shrugs and scoops up the little snake.
It shoots up her sleeve, vanishing into her blue hair to rejoin her siblings.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Hope you don't mind. She's been a bit shy ever since we were little.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That won't be a problem. I'll get it back to you in a few days. I just want to check if the study of ley lines can help with our aeroshell's force analysis.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Is that all? You could've left a message. No need to go out of your way.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Well, and I needed someone to unload a bit on. It's been months since I submitted our resupply application, and there doesn't appear to be any progress.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: This slow starvation for all of us is a waste of effort. They should just cut the cord and scrap all these projects they feel "show no value in the short term."

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Look at the silver lining. We're sure to get our new offices.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Office space, the one thing we have in abundance here.
She waves her arms in irritation before slipping back into her usual tone.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: *sigh* Anyway, how are things on your side? I'm free for the moment.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I'm progressing just fine. Take a look.
She steps closer to the desk. Hissabeth shifts some space and lays out the blueprints.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Excellent. Feel free to let me know if you require any help.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You know, for all the time we've worked together, there are still many questions left unanswered between us. I'm curious: why did you choose this project?
The tenor of their conversation has changed since their first meeting. This isn't a test. It's genuine concern.
Time has built enough trust between them to ask.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: There are many other teams pursuing the "combination of arcanum and science." I think one of them is presently working on cleaning incantations and plant-related rituals.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Why choose Plesetsk? Is it that you feel your expertise in material science will be of most benefit here? Or do you have a particular interest in the aerospace industry?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Don't mistake my intentions. I'm happy you chose to join our little team. You've performed exceptionally well so far.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: If I had to put a finger on it, I'd say it was curiosity. I really want to know where those Golden Records will end up.
She rolls up the blueprint before settling into a relaxed posture.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Remember what I told you about my parents? They were studying information technology at Laplace before the first "Storm" struck.
Hissabeth's mind has always jumped around, but now Pointer can keep up. She knows to wait for the point to come back around.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I can't wrap my head around that stuff. My whole life has been a constant stream of information. You wouldn't believe how distracting it is to have eight voices in your brain, bothering you night and day.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Still, all nine of us enjoyed reading. Whenever we found a particularly compelling article, we'd divide it up and each focus on a different part.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We'd always have a huge brainstorm after we finished. It was a lot of fun actually. *sigh* I miss those times.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I still remember the day that meteor fell to Earth.

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "Our latest reports are that Voyager 1 has officially traveled the furthest through our solar system of any man-made spacecraft ..."

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "Surpassing Pioneer 10 by a distance of approximately 69.419 astronomical units ..."

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I don't remember where I was or what I was doing, but I remember the broadcast was talking about the Voyager 1.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And that all nine of us were staring at the twinkling dot on the screen.

items.speaker: Little Hissabeth
items.text: If the moon is almost 400,000 kilometers away from us, how much further away was this little rock from Earth when it started on its journey?

items.speaker: Little Hissabeth
items.text: Unbelievable ...

Невероятно？
"Unbelievable"?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We never knew the stars above our heads could actually fall into our world.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What was happening up there? For all our brainstorms, we never reached the solid conclusion.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Where will Voyager 1 go? Who, if anyone, will find its Golden Records? When will the stars stop shining?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Are there researchers out there just like us living on another planet, looking for the same answers?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: One little meteor brought us so many questions, and we could never leave a stone unturned.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I see. That's why you joined this project, despite its lack of immediate contributions to society.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Nonsense! Our work is critical to the future of aerospace engineering. We've got plenty of contributions to offer.
This time, she's the one holding up a hand, waiting for a high five.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Was that an attempt to cheer me up? There's no need. I'm not easily discouraged.
Palm to palm, their hands meet for just a moment.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hmm. You've warmed up a bit.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Yeah, thanks to the 24/7 heating, and because I keep all of us well fed.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Speaking of, I'm headed to town to find a restaurant. Care to join me?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: There's some decent food in Plesetsk now, thanks to the new policies. Do you want anything in particular?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Your call.
Back then, we never thought to ask why our supply application had been put on ice for so long.
May 1987, Plesetsk Cosmodrome

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: They're terminating the project?!
The noise startles the snakes. One by one, they poke their heads out to join the shock.
Too bad the moment's already passed. Pointer doesn't even have time to snap a picture.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: I understand, ma'am, but you should know that our top priority after each "Storm" is to restore the Foundation and the LSCC to full function as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: With our current shortages of resources and manpower, that means cutting all non-essential projects.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Non-essential? Then what is it that counts as "essential"? Who decided on our priority?!
Before the snakes can hiss again in protest, Pointer reaches out and grabs Hissabeth.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Calm down, Hissabeth. I understand that Mr. Ludwig did his best to keep as many projects running in Plesetsk as he could. We couldn't have stayed here this long if it weren't for him.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But he's only a branch leader. He doesn't get to make the top-level decisions.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: They act as if all of their essential and valuable consumer technology just popped up out of nowhere!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: To think that aerospace engineering has less to contribute than their other projects?! S**t! They wouldn't even have vegetable packets in their instant noodles without us!

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: I'm sorry, but our decision is final.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Please allow me to finish. As you can imagine, I have several other meetings lined up after this.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Sure. Please continue.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Madam Lucy has expressed that she is not in favor of this decision. To that end, she asked me to deliver a "lifeline" for your work here.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: As you know, our knowledge about the "Storm" remains extremely limited. Madam Lucy believes we could better manage our circumstances if we could observe it in greater detail, particularly its extent.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: She's seeking volunteers from Plesetsk for a project, one that aims to send a monitor into space in order to collect data as the "Storm" arrives.
Two completely different reactions.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What about the other projects? Where will the researchers be assigned if their projects have all been terminated?
Pointer shoots her another look, trying to signal her. But Hissabeth either doesn't notice or doesn't care.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Most will be reassigned to other teams. I'm afraid there isn't much manpower to spare on our work here.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: That's the deal. If you want to stay on this project, then this mission must become your full focus. On the bright side, you'll have full access to all the resources left in Plesetsk.
He makes a quick glance down the hallway to check no one else is around, then steps closer and lowers his voice.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: I believe you two to be the most talented researchers in Plesetsk, and I know you want to achieve something with your work here.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Still, I think I should caution you against accepting this task. Sure, if you pull this off, you'd become a legend throughout our organization, but there's only so much value in fame and admiration.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And what would happen if we were to fail?

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: I'm afraid your best hope would be instant death, and it may be much worse than that. No one knows for certain what the "Storm" can do, after all.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: I'm not sure this is worth your lives.
Noticing another researcher approaching from the far end of the hall with luggage in hand, he steps back, readopting his cool professional tone.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher
items.text: Alright, that's all. I just need you to confirm that you've been informed. You'll have 24 hours to respond to our request.
After receiving the official documents, Pointer and Hissabeth return to their office.
They say nothing for a long time. The weight of the decision before them deserves their silent consideration. Finishing her deliberations, Pointer clears the air.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth, I know you're a big supporter of Madam Lucy, but I'm sure you agree this mission is a statistical death sentence.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: If you're struggling for a way to say no, I'll ...
Her words don't seem to have any purchase on her fellow researcher. Hissabeth looks up at her with a puzzled expression.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Sorry, what? Never mind. I've got good news.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I just talked to Windsong. She's got a solution to one of our major issues.
Hissabeth waves a hand as she answers, continuing her work.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Wait. Don't tell me you want to volunteer?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Why shouldn't we? This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But have you even considered the risk we'd be taking? Like the liaison said.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We'll have all the equipment we need, with a project that's progressing smoothly, working towards an achievable goal for the common good.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It is almost like the universe is within our grasp. All we must do is make our teleport disk work.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It's not that simple. We'd still need an astronaut capable of launching the monitor. Who could we find that would be capable of acclimatizing to a zero-gravity environment under high heat and pressure in such a short time?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: That's the good news! Windsong already found us an ideal candidate—an acrobat.
Hissabeth finishes her task and holds out the sheet to Pointer: a follow-up work schedule.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Here, I made a list of issues we'll need to tackle. Of course, that's only assuming you'll accept Madam Lucy's mission too.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I remember we talked about space exploration when I first arrived in Plesetsk. You said you wanted to know what's going on up there, too.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: So tell me, what price are you willing to pay for that answer?
Breathe. Let the air find its balance within.
Remember what Mr. Kozlov said: "You must never be afraid of falling." I just have to imagine myself floating in space.
That's right. I will not fall from the wire again.
The circus barker's introduction booms above the blinding lights, followed by a wave of cheers and applause.

items.speaker: Circus Barker
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, introducing our fabulous wire dancer, the youngest acrobat of the Utrennyaya Circus—

items.speaker: Circus Barker
items.text: Kiperina!
